description.value:
Duration 24 hours

If your Hollow is lost, stolen, or destroyed, the Quiet-state boons of the spirit last bound to it remain available to you for 24 hours, through sheer habit. You cannot Parley, go Unveiled, or prepare spells during this time — the boons persist, the appointment does not. At the end of the 24 hours the boons end whether or not you have recovered the Hollow or bound another.

cinderfall.incomplete: "Quiet-state boons persist for 24h" needs Quiet-state boons to have rule-element representation to persist under a special condition. Separately, no rule element anywhere in pf2e-source detects the loss, theft, or destruction of a specific held item as an activation condition for a different effect. Hollowbound's entire Toll / Fraying / Quiet-Unveiled / Parley system has zero rule-element representation anywhere in this corpus -- classes.hollowbound.json ships system.rules: [] and defines the whole subsystem only in flags.cinderfall prose (the terms array and progression table). Confirmed via grep -rli "SpecialResource" across feats/class/hollowbound/ and classes.hollowbound.json -> zero matches. Note: SpecialResource with renew:false IS a real, precedented mechanism for a manually-tracked, non-daily-refilling pool (confirmed live in this very corpus at feats/class/fleshmancer/fleshmancer.vitae-pool.json, max:10, renew:false) -- so this is not an engine limitation, but there is no equivalent "Toll Pool"-style classfeature card anywhere in feats/class/hollowbound/ to attach such a rule element to; a card would need to be authored first, which is out of scope for a gap-filling pass over the existing 75 cards.
